static_traits.name: Zhou Wei
static_traits.social_status: Having friends and family to confide in, but not yet discussing this problem with others; relationship with the surfing partner tense due to one's own negative interpretation
static_traits.medical_history: No similar problem experience before; not yet received psychotherapy before; no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe time and events concretely; rather negative emotional tone; cognitive tendencies of 'mind-reading' and 'jumping to conclusions'; fairly cooperative with the counselor, willing to try behavioral experiments; marked self-monitoring and self-reproach

basic_info.main_problem: I feel my surfing partner no longer surfs with me because they think I'm not good enough at surfing, which pains me and produces inadequacy.
basic_info.core_demands: These inadequacy feelings and self-doubt are affecting my enjoyment of surfing, so I decided to seek counseling.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough (insufficient ability)
My worth depends on what others think of my abilities

special_situations.event: About a month ago, the surfing partner stopped surfing with me
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others are unwilling to surf with me, it means my skills are not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Actively communicating with the partner to gain explanation and comfort
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They stopped going with me because I am not good enough

special_situations.event: Surfing alone in the sea; negative thoughts arise every time surfing alone
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If no one is willing to surf with me, it means I embarrass people and no one wants to approach me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding talking about this with others to avoid being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I must have embarrassed people by going surfing with them

special_situations.event: Last weekend falling off the wave (wipe out), with no one around seeing it at the time
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make mistakes on the wave, it proves my overall level is unqualified
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reinforcing self-criticism afterwards, trying to 'improve' performance through self-blame
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is why they do not want to go with me, I am not good enough

special_situations.event: The partner explaining that not going together is due to a busy schedule rather than my skill issues
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others' explanations contradict my worries, that's just a polite excuse and cannot explain the problem
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Insisting on privately speculating about others' thoughts rather than gathering more evidence
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just making excuses, embarrassed to say I'm no good

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be accepted and recognized, especially hoping to be seen as competent by peers in an important activity (surfing)
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being rejected and judged as not good enough, worrying about being belittled after exposing inadequacy
defense_goal: Reducing the risk of being directly negated through preemptive self-denial and cautious speculation about others' evaluations

object_relations.object_representation: Picky others who may negate oneself (such as the partner)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests more directly verifying the reason with the partner and designing a behavioral experiment
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client worries this will worsen the relationship and the other will confirm one is 'not good enough' (seeing others' potential feedback as a threat)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Expressing concerns in a hesitant, worried tone, using words like 'if / maybe / whether', avoiding immediate commitment and asking for scripts or prepared questions to gain a sense of control.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor emphasizes the lack of evidence and encourages examining facts (such as the partner truly being busy)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client attributing one's own 'not being accepted' feelings to others' negative views of oneself (believing the other is just making excuses)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing 'they are just politely saying they're busy', insisting on one's own interpretation, firm but uneasy tone, reducing in-depth discussion on factual evidence.

manifestations: The rejected experience of the partner no longer going together
Feeling lonely and self-doubtful when surfing alone in the sea
Linking technical mistakes (falling) with being negated by others
outcomes: Self-doubt and impaired sense of self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Believing the partner looks down on oneself, just making excuses not to surf together
Interpreting inner sense of not being accepted as others' true thoughts

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Repeated self-reproach and self-denial at sea
Worries that communicating with a partner will 'mess things up', hopes for scripts and question lists to reduce risk

exception_events.target_problem: In the partner's absence, the client usually engages in mind-reading speculation with self-doubt, leading to declining surfing experience and relationship tension
exception_events.unique_outcome: Once actively communicated with the partner about this, learning it was due to a busy schedule, not negation of skills; obtaining information different from one's own assumption
exception_events.reason: Different approach: actively communicating to verify the reason; different support: Fang Ming clearly giving a realistic interpretation (busy schedule)

positive_force: Willing to seek help and accept counseling, good cooperation
Willing to try behavioral experiments and script preparation, has action willingness
Able to identify one's own negative automatic thoughts (such as 'maybe I am not good enough')
Having some social support (friends and family)
negative_force: Marked tendency toward mind reading and jumping to conclusions
Negating positive information, reinforcing the belief of inadequacy
Excessive reliance on external evaluation to define self-worth
Self-monitoring and self-reproach shrinking the experience, avoiding direct contact

target_behavior.behavior: Repeated self-deprecation and mind-reading speculation while surfing (such as 'I am not good enough, they do not want to go with me'), with loneliness and self-doubt
antecedent: A partner stopped joining a month ago
Recalling the partner's explanation of being busy
target_behavior.core_reason: High sensitivity to being rejected and the cognitive bias of 'mind-reading / jumping to conclusions', plus over-relying on others' evaluations to define ability and self-worth
target_behavior.function: Self-protection and avoiding uncertainty: avoiding facing possible rejection and embarrassment through preemptive self-denial
target_behavior.consequence: Declining surfing pleasure, increased sense of loneliness, tense relationship with the partner, persistent self-doubt
